facts.fact_text: During the period from 2011 to 2013, all the applicants participated in a number of peaceful opposition demonstrations.
In the course of many of the peaceful opposition demonstrations, most of the applicants were arrested and subsequently convicted, as the assemblies had not been authorised.
The second applicant was arrested during a demonstration on 20 October 2012.
The third applicant was arrested during a demonstration on 20 October 2012.
The fourth applicant was arrested during a demonstration on 26 January 2013.
The fifth applicant was arrested during a demonstration on 26 January 2013.
The second applicant was arrested during a demonstration on 11 March 2013.
The fourth applicant was arrested during a demonstration on 11 March 2013.
According to the applicants, they had intended to participate in upcoming protests planned by Milli Shura, including a protest scheduled for 9 March 2014, which was eventually cancelled.
The fourth applicant was an organiser of a protest scheduled for 23 February 2014.
According to the fourth applicant, he had created a Facebook group calling for the resignation of the Baku city mayor.
According to the fourth applicant, the Baku city mayor had allegedly insulted the Azeri nation in a speech by saying that the only man in the country was the President.
The Facebook group created by the fourth applicant had invited the public to participate in a demonstration against the Baku city mayor.
All the applicants were arrested in either February or March 2014.
The fourth applicant was arrested on 22 February 2014.
The first applicant was arrested on 27 February 2014.
The second applicant was arrested on 27 February 2014.
The third applicant was arrested on 27 February 2014.
The sixth applicant was arrested on 5 March 2014.
The fifth applicant claimed that he had been arrested on 5 March 2014.
According to the official records, the fifth applicant was arrested early in the morning (at around 7 a.m.) on 6 March 2014.
According to the official records, the first applicant was arrested for disobeying a lawful order of a police officer to stop swearing loudly without addressing anyone in particular.
According to the official records, the police approached the second applicant because he had been noticed behaving suspiciously.
According to the official records, the police approached the sixth applicant because he had been noticed behaving suspiciously.
According to the official records, the police approached the third applicant because he was suspected of committing a traffic accident.
According to the official records, the police approached the fifth applicant because there was a complaint against him by a certain Ms K.N.
According to the official records, the police approached the fourth applicant because there was information about him.

According to the official records, the second applicant was arrested because when police officers had approached him, he had deliberately failed to comply with an order to produce an identity document and/or had been rude or showed resistance.

According to the official records, the sixth applicant was arrested because when police officers had approached him, he had deliberately failed to comply with an order to produce an identity document and/or had been rude or showed resistance.

All the applicants were charged with an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer).

Article 410.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 provided, at the material time, that a copy of the administrative-offence report shall be given to an individual who is subject to administrative-offence proceedings.
All the applicants were charged with an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer).
The courts sentenced the applicants to periods of administrative detention varying from ten to twenty days, as detailed in the Appendix.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe, titled 'The honouring of obligations and commitments by Azerbaijan', expressed concern that recently adopted amendments to the Criminal Code and the Administrative Code had increased penalties for the organisers of, and participants in, unauthorised gatherings.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that, considering the authorities' ongoing blanket ban on protests in the Baku city centre, the amendments increasing penalties for organisers of and participants in unauthorised gatherings were likely to have a further negative impact on freedom of assembly and freedom of expression.
Resolution 2062 (2015) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe, titled 'The functioning of democratic institutions in Azerbaijan', was adopted on 23 June 2015.

Resolution 2062 (2015) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that the lack of independence of the judiciary remains a concern in Azerbaijan, where the executive branch is alleged to continue to exert undue influence.
Resolution 2062 (2015) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that dubiously motivated criminal prosecutions and disproportionate sentences remain a concern in Azerbaijan.

Resolution 2062 (2015) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that fairness of trials, equality of arms and respect for the presumption of innocence are major concerns in Azerbaijan.

Resolution 2062 (2015) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that it was alarmed by reports by human rights defenders and international NGOs, confirmed by the Council of Europe Commissioner for Human Rights, concerning the increase in criminal prosecutions against NGO leaders, journalists, lawyers and others who express critical opinions, based on alleged charges in relation to their work.

Resolution 2062 (2015) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe called on the Azerbaijani authorities to end the systemic harassment of those who are critical of the government and to release those wrongfully detained.

The European Parliament in its Resolution (2015/2840(RSP)) of 10 September 2015 emphasised that the overall human rights situation in Azerbaijan has deteriorated continuously over the last few years, with growing intimidation and repression and intensification of the practice of criminal prosecution of NGO leaders, human rights defenders, journalists and other civil society representatives.
The European Parliament in its Resolution (2015/2840(RSP)) of 10 September 2015 emphasised that peaceful protesters have been effectively banned from demonstrating in central Baku since 2006.

The European Parliament in its Resolution (2015/2840(RSP)) of 10 September 2015 emphasised that new, harsh fines and longer periods of administrative detention for those who organise or participate in unauthorised public gatherings have recently been introduced in Azerbaijan.

Amnesty International in its Report of May 2014, titled 'Behind Bars: Silencing Dissent in Azerbaijan', referred to a decrease of public protests in Azerbaijan due to the harshening from 1 January 2013 of penalties for breach of rules on organisation and holding of peaceful assemblies.

Amnesty International in its Report of May 2014, titled 'Behind Bars: Silencing Dissent in Azerbaijan', emphasised that those who have called for public protest in Azerbaijan have been dealt with harshly, with criminal proceedings initiated against them under fabricated charges.

In a public statement of 7 March 2014, titled 'Azerbaijan: Opposition party loses HQ after explosion and sees seven members arrested within 2 weeks', Amnesty International reported on numerous detentions and arrests of activists of the Popular Front Party of Azerbaijan during late February and early March 2014.
Amnesty International's public statement of 7 March 2014 reported on an explosion which occurred on 3 March 2014 in the basement of a building housing the Popular Front Party of Azerbaijan.

Amnesty International's public statement of 7 March 2014 reported on allegations by the owner of the property housing the Popular Front Party of Azerbaijan that prior to the explosion he had been pressured to evict the party.
According to the applicants, they were not given access to a lawyer after their arrest or while they were in police custody.

According to a record (protokol) issued by a police officer who had arrested the fifth applicant and prepared an administrative offence report on him, a State-funded lawyer was proposed to the fifth applicant, but the fifth applicant refused his assistance.
The record (protokol) regarding the fifth applicant was signed by the police officer and the fifth applicant.
The lawyer's name and signature are missing from the record (protokol) regarding the fifth applicant.
According to a statement (ərizə) written by the fourth applicant at a police office on the day of his arrest, the fourth applicant had refused the services of a lawyer.
According to all the applicants, they were not given an opportunity to appoint lawyers of their own choosing during the court proceedings before the first-instance courts.
State-funded lawyers were appointed to assist the applicants during the court proceedings before the first-instance courts.
According to the documents in the respective case files, the first applicant refused the assistance of a State-funded lawyer and decided to defend himself in person before the first-instance court.
According to the documents in the respective case files, the third applicant refused the assistance of a State-funded lawyer and decided to defend himself in person before the first-instance court.
According to the documents in the respective case files, the fifth applicant refused the assistance of a State-funded lawyer and decided to defend himself in person before the first-instance court.
According to the documents in the respective case files, the sixth applicant refused the assistance of a State-funded lawyer and decided to defend himself in person before the first-instance court.

According to the transcripts of the respective hearings, the State-funded lawyer for the second applicant, Mr K.K., briefly asked the court to discontinue the administrative case against the second applicant.
According to the transcripts of the respective hearings, the State-funded lawyer for the fourth applicant, Ms S.H., briefly asked the court to consider the young age of the fourth applicant.
In their statements before the courts, the first, second, third, fourth and sixth applicants contested the police officers' versions of the events surrounding their arrests.
The first applicant argued before the court that he had been arrested for his political activity.
The third applicant argued before the court that the police's allegation that they were investigating a car accident was a lie and that the police had wanted to frame him.
The fourth applicant argued before the court that he had been arrested for the comments he had posted on Facebook against the Baku city mayor.
The courts disregarded the applicants' statements contesting the police officers' versions of the events.
The fifth applicant gave a self-incriminatory statement before the court confirming the police officers' account of the events.

The fifth applicant subsequently claimed that he had given the self-incriminatory statement because the previous day he had been threatened with more serious charges and had still felt under the control of the police.

During the hearings with regard to the first applicant, only the police officers who, according to the official records, had arrested the first applicant and/or issued administrative offence reports on him were questioned as witnesses.

During the hearings with regard to the second applicant, only the police officers who, according to the official records, had arrested the second applicant and/or issued administrative offence reports on him were questioned as witnesses.

During the hearings with regard to the fourth applicant, only the police officers who, according to the official records, had arrested the fourth applicant and/or issued administrative offence reports on him were questioned as witnesses.

During the hearings with regard to the fifth applicant, only the police officers who, according to the official records, had arrested the fifth applicant and/or issued administrative offence reports on him were questioned as witnesses.
In their statements, the police officers questioned as witnesses reiterated the official version of the reasons for the applicants' arrests.
In the case of the third applicant, the court questioned three prosecution witnesses.

All three prosecution witnesses in the case of the third applicant stated that the third applicant had argued with the police officers, resisted and insulted them, saying to a police major 'why have you brought these puppies here?'
In the case of the sixth applicant, the court did not question any witnesses.
The courts found that the applicants had committed the administrative offences attributed to them.
The courts convicted the applicants under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer).
The courts sentenced the applicants to periods of administrative detention varying from ten to twenty days, as detailed in the Appendix.
The first applicant was also convicted under Article 296 of the Code of Administrative Offences (minor hooliganism).
On various dates the applicants lodged appeals with the Baku Court of Appeal, presenting their version of the facts surrounding their arrests.

The first, second, third, fifth and sixth applicants argued before the Baku Court of Appeal that they had been unlawfully arrested for their political activity, including their active participation in demonstrations.
The fourth applicant argued before the Baku Court of Appeal that he had been unlawfully arrested for the comments he had posted on social media.
The applicants complained before the Baku Court of Appeal that the hearings before the respective first-instance courts had not been fair.
The fifth applicant submitted to the Baku Court of Appeal that previously he had given self-incriminatory statements for fear of being framed for the offence of illegal possession of drugs.
The fifth applicant complained to the Baku Court of Appeal that he had been kept in the police station overnight from 5 to 6 March 2014 without any official decision or record of his detention.
All the applicants were represented before the Baku Court of Appeal by lawyers of their own choosing.

On various dates the Baku Court of Appeal dismissed the applicants' appeals and upheld the decisions of the respective first-instance courts, stating that the conclusions reached by those courts were correct, as detailed in the Appendix.
